summary: Same animation and same rendering math (static midpoint-displacement heightfield -> HSV value, hue = offset + speed*t + height*paletteWidth, instant map regeneration on a timer), but the port ships two wrong defaults (PaletteWidth 1.0 vs 0.15, so untouched it is a full rainbow instead of the original's red-orange fire band; MapLifetime 8.05 s vs 5.05 s) and two wrong dial responses (Roughness is inverted; Speed is linear where the original is hyperbolic).
observations: Rig: 60 px strip. Both sides alive, no compile/runtime errors, wantsSensors false on both. Steady at t=120-150 s (--label late): orig brightnessTrend steady, port steady, zeroMotionFrames 0 on both. No decay, freeze or saturation on either side.

Shared mechanism confirmed by --dump: within a map epoch each pixel's MAX channel (HSV value) is byte-constant while the hue rotates uniformly; the terrain is a static 1D heightfield redrawn instantly at regeneration. Both sides behave this way, so the animation is 'frozen terrain + hue sweep', not morphing terrain.

Hue relation is identical on both sides: dumping at --controls sliderPaletteWidth=1 shows hue(pixel) - hue(pixel0) == height(pixel)/255 - height(pixel0)/255 on BOTH orig and port (checked over 10 pixels, agreement to +/-0.01 cycles). Same sign, same scaling.

COLOR AT UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS IS THE BIG VISIBLE DIFFERENCE. Original: meanB is exactly 0 in every captured frame (baseline, 120 frames), hue confined to 0-60 deg — a black->red->orange->yellow fire ramp. Port: full 360 deg rainbow, all three channels active (meanR/G/B all ~68 in baseline). Bisecting the PaletteWidth dial pins it exactly: orig untouched px0..5 at t=17.00 = ff9a00 bd4700 7c1200 271d00 362b00 453a00, which is BYTE-IDENTICAL to orig rendered with sliderPaletteWidth=0.15; the port's untouched render is byte-identical to its own sliderPaletteWidth=1 render. So the original's default PaletteWidth is 0.15 and the port's is 1.0.

MAP LIFETIME DEFAULT IS 1.6x TOO LONG. At --fps 20 over 40 s the original regenerates at t = 5.00, 10.05, 15.10, 20.15, 25.20, 30.25, 35.30 (period 5.05 s); the port at t = 8.00, 16.05, 24.10, 32.15 (period 8.05 s). Confirmed fps-invariant (5 fps survey: 5.2 s vs 8.2 s, i.e. one survey frame of quantisation). Both regenerate in a SINGLE frame with no crossfade (dump at 4.90/4.95/5.00 on orig and 7.95/8.00 on port shows the whole height profile swapping between two consecutive frames).

ROUGHNESS DIAL IS INVERTED. Terrain statistics (mean |height difference| between adjacent pixels / count of local extrema per 60-px frame, averaged over 5 maps): orig 0 -> 25.2/19.6, 0.25 -> 20.2/15.6, 0.5 -> 12.9/11.0, 0.75 -> 7.6/7.8, 1 -> 6.3/2.8 (monotonically SMOOTHER as the slider rises). Port 0 -> 9.9/4.4, 0.25 -> 10.6/7.8, 0.5 -> 13.9/19.6, 0.75 -> 31.1/34.6, 1 -> 47.5/37.4 (monotonically ROUGHER). The two curves run in opposite directions and cross near 0.5.

SPEED DIAL RESPONSE CURVE DIFFERS, though the defaults coincide. Hue rotation rate measured by unwrapping the hue of the brightest pixel over 0.5 s at 20 fps, PaletteWidth pinned to 1: orig fits rate = 0.1525/(1 - speed) exactly (speed 0 -> 0.152, 0.25 -> 0.205, 0.5 -> 0.305, 0.75 -> 0.610, 0.85 -> 1.020, 0.90 -> 1.527, 0.95 -> 3.058 cyc/s; at speed = 1 the original degenerates to a frozen hue 0.000 with motion 0). Port fits rate = 0.05 + 1.00*speed (0 -> 0.051, 0.25 -> 0.299, 0.5 -> 0.549, 0.75 -> 0.799, 0.85 -> 0.899, 0.90 -> 0.951, 0.95 -> 1.000, 1 -> 1.049 cyc/s). Port is 3.0x too slow at speed 0, 1.8x too FAST at 0.5, and 3.1x too slow at 0.95.

Default hue speed MATCHES: untouched (PaletteWidth pinned to 1 only) orig 0.510 cyc/s vs port 0.500 cyc/s — i.e. orig default Speed ~= 0.70 on its hyperbolic curve, port default ~= 0.45 on its linear one, landing at the same rate.
Both sides are TIME-BASED, not frame-stepped: hue rate measured at 10/20/40 fps is orig 0.509/0.510/0.508 and port 0.500/0.500/0.499 cyc/s. No frame-rate coupling on either side.
PaletteOffset is IDENTICAL on both sides: a uniform hue shift of exactly +0.25 cycles per +0.25 of slider, wrapping at 1.0 (offset 0 and offset 1 render identically on both).

MapLifetime DIAL mapping is IDENTICAL on both sides even though the default differs: regeneration period ~= 30 s * slider value on both (0.25 -> 7.6 s both, 0.5 -> 15.1 s both, 0.75 -> 22.6 s both, 1 -> 30.1 s both; at 0 neither side regenerates within 60 s).

Port terrain is somewhat finer-grained at defaults. Mean adjacent |diff| / extrema per frame over 9 maps: orig 14.3/14.2, port 15.1/19.3 (seed 1); seed 7 orig 11.8/13.9 vs port 15.1/22.7; seed 1234 orig 11.6/12.6 vs port 14.2/21.0. Consistently ~50% more local extrema on the port.

MaxLevel/DetailLevel dial runs the same DIRECTION on both but the port over-responds by roughly one octave. With Roughness pinned to 0.5, extrema per frame: orig 0 -> 0.0, 0.25 -> 0.6, 0.5 -> 1.4, 0.75 -> 2.8, 1 -> 11.0; port 0 -> 1.0, 0.25 -> 1.0, 0.5 -> 3.2, 0.75 -> 12.6, 1 -> 18.4. Port at 0.75 already exceeds the original's maximum detail.

CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH (2 of 6 names): original exposes sliderMaxLevel (label 'MaxLevel') and slidermapLifetime (label 'mapLifetime', lower-case m); the port exposes sliderDetailLevel (label 'DetailLevel') and sliderMapLifetime (label 'MapLifetime'). The other four (sliderSpeed, sliderPaletteWidth, sliderPaletteOffset, sliderRoughness) match in name and kind. All 12 controls are sliders and all 12 probe responsive with 0 and 1 differing from each other.

With all six dials explicitly matched (level 0.6, mapLifetime 0.25, speed 0.7, paletteWidth 0.15, paletteOffset 0.3, roughness 0.5) the 40 s / 10 fps waterfalls are a convincing match: same green fire band, same ~7.6 s map blocks, same slow-hue-band rhythm, same ridge-and-valley silhouette character; the only residual is the port's slightly finer terrain.

dials.name: MaxLevel (orig: sliderMaxLevel) / DetailLevel (port: sliderDetailLevel)
dials.origEffect: Sets subdivision depth of the heightfield. Local extrema per 60-px frame (Roughness pinned 0.5): 0.0 at slider 0 (a single smooth hump), 0.6 / 1.4 / 2.8 / 11.0 at 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.
dials.portEffect: Same direction, but shifted up about one octave: 1.0 / 1.0 / 3.2 / 12.6 / 18.4 at the same settings. Port's 0.75 already matches the original's 1.0, and the port's top end is ~1.7x more detailed than the original's.

dials.name: mapLifetime (orig: slidermapLifetime) / MapLifetime (port: sliderMapLifetime)
dials.origEffect: Regeneration period ~= 30 s * value (0.25 -> 7.6 s, 0.5 -> 15.1 s, 0.75 -> 22.6 s, 1 -> 30.1 s; 0 -> no regeneration inside 60 s). Untouched default gives 5.05 s.
dials.portEffect: Identical mapping (7.6 / 15.1 / 22.6 / 30.1 s, none at 0). Only the UNTOUCHED default differs: 8.05 s instead of 5.05 s.

dials.name: sliderSpeed
dials.origEffect: Hyperbolic: hue rate = 0.1525 / (1 - speed) cyc/s. 0.152 at 0, 0.305 at 0.5, 1.53 at 0.9, 3.06 at 0.95, and at exactly 1.0 the pattern degenerates to a frozen hue 0 (motion 0).
dials.portEffect: Linear: hue rate = 0.05 + 1.00 * speed cyc/s. 0.051 at 0, 0.549 at 0.5, 0.951 at 0.9, 1.049 at 1.0, never degenerate. Matches the original only near the default (both ~0.50 cyc/s untouched).

dials.name: sliderPaletteWidth
dials.origEffect: Controls how many hue degrees the height range spans. 0 -> flat 0 deg (pure red, brightness-only), 0.25 -> 0-90 deg, 0.5 -> 0-179 deg, 0.75 -> 0-269 deg, 1 -> full 0-359 deg. Untouched default is 0.15 (a ~54 deg red->yellow fire band).
dials.portEffect: Byte-for-byte the same mapping at every value tested (0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1 give the same hue spans). Only the UNTOUCHED default differs: 1.0 (full rainbow) instead of 0.15.

dials.name: sliderPaletteOffset
dials.origEffect: Uniform hue rotation of the whole strip: exactly +0.25 cycles per +0.25 of slider, wrapping (offset 1 == offset 0).
dials.portEffect: Identical: same +0.25 cycles per 0.25, same wrap.

dials.name: sliderRoughness
dials.origEffect: INVERSE convention (higher slider = smoother terrain). Mean adjacent |height diff| / extrema per frame: 25.2/19.6 at 0, 20.2/15.6 at 0.25, 12.9/11.0 at 0.5, 7.6/7.8 at 0.75, 6.3/2.8 at 1.
dials.portEffect: Opposite direction (higher slider = rougher): 9.9/4.4 at 0, 10.6/7.8 at 0.25, 13.9/19.6 at 0.5, 31.1/34.6 at 0.75, 47.5/37.4 at 1. Also a wider dynamic range than the original's.

feedback: Fix the default PaletteWidth: the port defaults to 1.0 (full 360 deg rainbow); the original defaults to 0.15, a narrow red->orange->yellow band with the blue channel at exactly 0 in every frame. This is the single most visible difference — untouched, the original looks like fire and the port looks like a rainbow. The dial itself is already exactly right (orig at 0.15 == orig untouched, byte-identical), so only the initial value needs changing.

Fix the default MapLifetime: the port regenerates the heightfield every 8.05 s, the original every 5.05 s (measured at 20 fps over 40 s). The dial-to-period mapping already matches on both sides (~30 s * slider value), so only the starting value is wrong — the original's default corresponds to slider ~0.168, the port's to ~0.267.

INVERT the Roughness slider. On the original, Roughness=0 gives the JAGGED terrain (mean adjacent |height diff| 25.2, ~20 local extrema per 60-px frame) and Roughness=1 gives the SMOOTHEST (6.3, ~3 extrema). The port does the exact opposite (0 -> 9.9/4.4, 1 -> 47.5/37.4). Mapping the slider to (1 - value) would put the direction right; after that, also check the range — the port's extremes (9.9..47.5) are wider than the original's (6.3..25.2), so the port at 1 is nearly 2x rougher than the original ever gets at 0.

Reshape the Speed dial from linear to hyperbolic. Original hue rate = 0.1525 / (1 - Speed) cycles/s; port is 0.05 + 1.00 * Speed. They agree only at the defaults. Concretely the port must be ~3x faster at Speed=0 (0.152 vs 0.051 cyc/s), ~1.8x SLOWER at Speed=0.5 (0.305 vs 0.549), and must blow up near 1 (original: 1.53 cyc/s at 0.9, 3.06 at 0.95, and frozen hue 0 exactly at 1.0). Whatever new curve is used, keep the untouched default at ~0.51 cyc/s, which is where the port already sits.

Rename two controls to the original's names/labels: sliderDetailLevel -> sliderMaxLevel (label 'MaxLevel') and sliderMapLifetime -> slidermapLifetime (label 'mapLifetime', lower-case m — the original really does spell it that way). The other four names already match.

Trim the DetailLevel/MaxLevel range by about one subdivision level. At Roughness=0.5 the original's extrema-per-frame across the slider are 0.0 / 0.6 / 1.4 / 2.8 / 11.0 while the port's are 1.0 / 1.0 / 3.2 / 12.6 / 18.4 — the port's 0.75 already equals the original's 1.0, and the port never reaches the original's completely straight single-hump look at slider 0 (original: 0 local extrema, port: 1).

After the roughness/level fixes, re-check the default terrain grain: at defaults the port averages ~19-23 local extrema per 60-px frame across seeds 1/7/1234 versus the original's ~13-14, so the port's untouched terrain is about 50% wigglier even before the dials are touched.

Everything else is already right and should not be disturbed: static-heightfield-plus-rotating-hue rendering, hue = offset + speed*t + height*paletteWidth with the same sign and scale, single-frame (no crossfade) map regeneration, PaletteOffset behaviour, the MapLifetime dial mapping, time-based (fps-invariant) animation at 10/20/40 fps, and a stable steady state out to t=150 s.
